category_title: Preschoolers who struggle with sharing objects during collaborative tasks
minimal_context: Darin and a friend are using different materials to build a castle together during a 10-minute center time activity.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Darin and Alex, please use these different materials to build a castle together.

STUDENT: (Takes blocks from Alex's pile) Give me that.

TUTOR: Alex is asking for a block to help build.

STUDENT: I had that first.

TUTOR: Remember to share your materials so you can finish the castle.

STUDENT: (Hides the blocks behind his back) That's mine!

options.A: Before center time begins, role-play sharing exchanges with a hand puppet, sometimes asking Darin to teach the puppet how to share.
options.B: Use a 5-point visual check-in chart matching numbers, colors, and faces to feeling words (from 1: calm/happy to 5: super angry) to assess his anxiety.
options.C: Let Darin continue working on the castle with his friend without making any further comment during the center time activity.
options.D: Redirect Darin to the castle-building task fairly quickly and emphasize the importance of staying focused on the center time activity.
